source.name: sp_ProcessOrder

assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
Tables dbo.Products, dbo.Orders, and dbo.OrderItems exist with compatible column definitions
Products.ProductID is the primary key or has a unique constraint
Orders.OrderID is a SERIAL or has a default value from a sequence
The OUTPUT parameter @OrderID is converted to INOUT parameter p_OrderID
PostgreSQL procedures automatically handle transaction boundaries - explicit BEGIN/COMMIT removed
SCOPE_IDENTITY() is replaced with RETURNING clause which is the PostgreSQL idiomatic approach
Custom error code 50001 is mapped to PostgreSQL ERRCODE 'P0001' (raise_exception)
NULL check added for product lookup as PostgreSQL SELECT INTO doesn't raise error on no rows

reviewFlags.reason: SQL Server OUTPUT parameters map to INOUT in PostgreSQL procedures. Verify calling code can handle INOUT semantics. If calling from application code, the parameter must be passed in both directions.
SCOPE_IDENTITY() replaced with RETURNING clause. Verify that Orders.OrderID has a default value (SERIAL, IDENTITY, or sequence default) to auto-generate the ID.
Generic exception handler catches all errors. In PostgreSQL procedures, transactions are automatically rolled back on exceptions. Verify this matches the desired error handling behavior.
Added explicit NULL check for product lookup. SQL Server sets variable to NULL if no rows found, PostgreSQL raises NO_DATA_FOUND. Verify this behavior matches business requirements.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures (PROCEDURE) automatically start a transaction and commit on success or rollback on exception. Explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are removed as they are implicit. If called within an existing transaction, the procedure participates in that transaction.

SQL Server OUTPUT parameters are converted to INOUT in PostgreSQL. The calling code must pass a variable that can receive the output value. The parameter must be provided even if the initial value is not used.
SCOPE_IDENTITY() is replaced with RETURNING clause, which is the PostgreSQL standard. This requires the OrderID column to have a default value (typically SERIAL or GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY).

SQL Server custom error 50001 is mapped to PostgreSQL ERRCODE 'P0001' (raise_exception). Application error handling code may need adjustment to handle PostgreSQL SQLSTATE codes instead of SQL Server error numbers.
SET NOCOUNT ON is removed as it has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL procedures do not return row count messages to the client by default.
